subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It is a fact that the same judgement can often __be taken by more than__ one way.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"in"** means expressing the situation of something that is or appears to be enclosed or surrounded by something else. (में)

 
 
• **Example: **The cat is** in **the box.
 
 
 
• **"In"** is used to indicate inclusion within space, a place, or limits. (में)
 
 
• **Example: **She is **in** the house.
 
 

Hence, using** "in"** makes the sentence grammatically** correct and coherent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: "be taken on more than"** (से अधिक पर लिया जाना): This does not fit well in the context of the sentence.

 
 
• **Example:** The decision can **be taken on more than** one occasion.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "be taken for more than"** (से अधिक के लिए लिया जाना): This phrase generally implies being mistaken for something else.
 
 
• **Example: **He was **taken for more than** just a teacher; he was a mentor.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "be taken of more than"** (से अधिक का लिया जाना): This phrase is awkward and not grammatically correct in this context.
 
 
• **Example:** The photograph was taken of more than just the landscape.
 
 

344:Td17,

The correct answer is **Option 1)**
